published.citation: Roy et al. 2022, dayside brightness temperature at 3.6 µm, 1463 +183 -196 K: 1463 +/- 196 K, https://arxiv.org/abs/2211.11793

temperature.note: Its day side's brightness temperature is measured in secondary eclipse at 3.6 µm (Spitzer IRAC) and nobody has imaged it, so the color is a Planck spectrum at its published temperature.
temperature.chosen: of the two bands, the one with the smaller relative uncertainty; the larger of its two errors is kept
